questions.question: Which of the following CANNOT be called a Debt instrument as referred in financial transactions?
questions.solution: Debt instruments are the assets that require a fixed payment with interest to the holder. Its examples include mortgages and bonds (corporate or government). Stocks cannot be called a Debt instrument.

questions.solution:

questions.question: Who formulated ‘the atomic theory’ of a matter?
questions.solution: ‘The atomic theory’ of a matter is a scientific theory that tells about the nature of matter. It states that matter is composed of units called atoms. John Dalton first formulated this theory, however, the existence of an atom was first suggested by Democritus.

questions.question: Which of the following type of medicine is used for treating indigestion?
questions.solution:
• Antacids are used for treating indigestion. They neutralize excess stomach acid to relieve sour stomach, heartburn, stomach upset, and acid indigestion.
 
• Antibiotics are used to treat diseases caused by bacteria,.
 
• Analgesics are painkillers which are used to treat pain and fever.
 
• Antiseptics are used to reduce the possibility of any sepsis or infection.

questions.question: Trypsin is present in which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Pancreatic juice**

__**Explanation:**__

__
 
• The pancreas secretes a liquid substance called** pancreatic juice**, which contains digestive enzymes.
 
• Trypsinogen, chymotrypsinogen, procarboxypeptidases, amylases, lipases, and nucleases are among the inactive enzymes found in the pancreatic juice secreted by the pancreas.
 
• These enzymes help in the breakdown of all food components that require digestion.
 
• **Enterokinase**, an enzyme secreted by the intestinal mucosa, converts trypsinogen into active trypsin.
 
• **Trypsin **helps to convert proteins into peptones.
 
• **Chymotrypsinogen** is a degrading enzyme that breaks down proteins into smaller peptides.
 
• **Procarboxypeptidases** enzymes remove C-terminal amino acids from peptides and proteins
 
• **Amylase **enzyme converts starch to maltose.
 
• **Lipase** is a digestive enzyme that breaks down fats into glycerol and fatty acids.
 
• **Nucleases** enzymes are specifically designed to break down the nucleotides that make up DNA and RNA.

**Conclusion:**__

**Trypsin **is found in the digestive system. It hydrolyzes proteins. It is present in the pancreatic juice and formed in the small intestine.

questions.question: Leeuwenhoek discovered the free living cells for the first time in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leeuwenhoek**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• Antonie van Leeuwenhoek

 
• He is also known for the discovery of **bacteria**.

 
 
• He is regarded as the father of microbiology. 
 
• Anton van Leeuwenhoek laid the foundation of plant anatomy and studied animal reproduction in detail.
 
• He was a Dutch microscopist and biologist born in Delft, **Netherlands**.
 
• He experimented with and observed microscopic organisms in the year **1676**.
 
• He is probably best known for his refinement of the **microscope**.
 
• He increased the magnifying power of the microscope from **20x **to **270x**.
 
• He was the first to observe bacteria and protozoa with his **single-lensed microscope**.
 
• In **1674**, he observed small single-celled organisms and named them '**Animalcules**'.
 
• In **1677,** he discovered **sperm in mammals**. 
 
• He was also the first person to study blood vessels and discovered blood cells and nematodes living in blood.

questions.question: The SI unit of G, the universal gravitation constant is ________.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Universal Gravitational Law:

__
 
• Sir Isaac Newton put forward the universal law of gravitation in 1687 and used it to explain the observed motions of the planets and moons.
 
• Newton’s Law of Universal Gravitation states that every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with force directly proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af29db6e88d3dfe751d03229d3799368f6d80c947fefdc04b7a11d356dc730f7.png] 

 
 
• Formula, Force, F=(GM₁M₂)/(r²)where, F is the gravitational force between bodies, M1 and M2 are the masses of the bodies, r is the distance between the centers of two bodies, and 8G is the universal gravitational constant.
 
• Here, G = 6.673 x 10-11 N m2/kg2.
 
• 
 
​Acceleration due to gravity:

 
 
• Acceleration due to gravity is the acceleration gained by an object due to gravitational force.
 
• Its SI unit is m/s2. It has both magnitude and direction, hence, it’s a vector quantity.
 
• Acceleration due to gravity is represented by g.
 
• The standard value of g on the surface of the earth at sea level is 9.8 m/s2.

Explanation:__

 
• The gravitational constant is the proportionality constant used in Newton’s Law of Gravitation and is commonly denoted by G.
 
• **The value of G in the SI system is 6.674 × 10−¹¹N m2kg–².**

questions.question: The power of an earthquake is expressed in terms of a magnitude on a scale called ________ scale.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Richter**

**CONCEPT:**

__
 
• **The power of an earthquake is expressed in terms of a magnitude on a scale called the Richter scale.**__
 
• The Richter scale was developed by Charles F. Richter and is used to measure the strength or magnitude of an earthquake.

__Explanation:__

Earthquake: An earthquake is a sudden shaking or trembling of the earth which lasts for a very short time. It is caused by a disturbance deep inside the earth’s crust.

 
• An earthquake is measured with a machine called a seismograph. The power of an earthquake is expressed in terms of magnitude on a scale called the Richter scale.
 
• An earthquake of 2.0 or less can be felt only a little.
 
• An earthquake over 5.0 can cause damage from things falling.
 
• A 6.0 or higher magnitude is considered very strong and 7.0 is classified as a major earthquake.
 
• Really destructive earthquakes have magnitudes higher than 7 on the Richter scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/14a95093f70204497d807bd98ba9be1318ae24b1c5852285fd197a44adb02aa2.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68a5f7892446d2db1ea92192e705e47a9f7764c05df8b751eee8cc23d4b3a3d1.png] 

 
• Richter scale is not linear. This means that an earthquake of magnitude 6 does not have one and a half times the destructive energy of an earthquake of magnitude 4.
 
• In fact, an increase of 2 in magnitude means 1000 times more destructive energy. Therefore, an earthquake of magnitude 6 has a thousand times more destructive energy than an earthquake of magnitude 4.
